items.title: Section: Wealth-and-Respect Veneration — Bowing, Circling, and Every Material Offering Named in Full

items.zh: 若諸菩薩，於如來所、若制多所，以諸衣服、飲食、臥具、病緣醫藥供身什物，敬問、禮拜、奉迎、合掌，種種熏香、末香、塗香、華鬘、伎樂、幢蓋、幡燈，歌頌稱讚，五輪歸命，趨遶右旋，而為供養。或復奉施無盡財供，或復奉施末尼、真珠、琉璃、䗍貝、璧玉、珊瑚、車𤦲、馬碯、虎魄金銀、赤珠、右旋如是等寶，或復奉施末尼、環玔、寶璩、印等諸莊嚴具，乃至奉施種種寶鈴，或散珍奇、或纏寶縷而為供養。是名菩薩於如來所、若制多所財敬供養。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who, in the Tathāgata's presence or at a shrine, offer robes, food and drink, bedding, and medicine for illness, along with every article supporting the body; who respectfully inquire, prostrate, welcome, and join their palms; who offer every kind of fragrant incense, powdered incense, and fragrant unguent, garlands of flowers, music and dance, banners, canopies, and lamps; who chant praises, prostrate with all five limbs in total self-surrender, and circle in reverence to the right — all of this constitutes veneration. Or again, bodhisattvas offer inexhaustible wealth as an offering; or offer maṇi jewels, pearls, lapis lazuli, conch shells, alabaster, coral, giant clam shell, agate, amber, gold and silver, red pearls, right-turning conches, and every jewel of this kind; or offer maṇi jewels, bracelets, jade ornaments, and seals as ornamental articles, down to offering every kind of jewelled bell, or scattering rare and marvellous objects, or offering robes woven through with jewelled thread. This is called a bodhisattva's wealth-and-respect veneration in the Tathāgata's presence or at a shrine.

items.title: Section: Vast Veneration's Sevenfold Structure — a Privilege Reserved for Bodhisattvas of the First Ground

items.zh: 若諸菩薩，於如來所、若制多所，長時施設即上所陳財敬供養，若多供具、若妙供具、若現在前、不現在前、若自造作、教他造作、若淳淨心猛利勝解現前供養；即以如是所種善根，迴向無上正等菩提，如是七種說名菩薩廣大供養。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who, in the Tathāgata's presence or at a shrine, set out the wealth-and-respect veneration already described above over a long period of time — whether through many offerings or exquisite offerings, whether present or absent, whether self-performed or taught to others, or whether offered with a genuinely pure mind and vivid, forceful conviction directly before the object of veneration — and then dedicate whatever wholesome root has thereby been planted towards supreme, complete awakening: these seven together are called a bodhisattva's vast veneration.

items.title: Section: Undefiled Veneration's Six Marks — No Contempt, No Pretence, and No Impure Substance

items.zh: 若諸菩薩，於如來所、若制多所，自手供養不懷輕慢；令他供養；不住放逸、懈惰、不敬而為供養；不輕棄擲、不散慢心、無雜染心而為供養；不於信佛國王、大臣、諸貴勝前，為財敬故，詐設種種虛事供養；不雌黃塗，不酥灌洗，不以種種局崛羅香、遏迦花等餘不淨物而為供養。如是六種說名菩薩無染供養。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who, in the Tathāgata's presence or at a shrine, venerate with their own hands without any trace of contempt; who also let others venerate; who never venerate while heedless, lazy, or disrespectful; who never venerate by carelessly discarding or scattering the offering, and never with a distracted or defiled mind; who never stage false, elaborate displays of veneration before kings, ministers, or other noble patrons who have faith in the Buddha, purely to win wealth or esteem for themselves; and who never venerate using orpiment paste, ghee-washing, or other impure substances such as guggulu incense or arka flowers as an offering — these six together are called a bodhisattva's undefiled veneration.

items.title: Section: Emanation-Body Veneration — the Eighth-Ground Bodhisattva Who Venerates With a Hundred Thousand Multiplied Hands

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，如是財敬、廣大、無染供養如來及制多時，或自臂力所集財寶，或從他求所獲財寶，或得眾具自在財寶，能為如是種種供養。已得眾具自在菩薩，化作化身，或一或二，或復眾多，乃至百千俱胝等數。此一切身皆於如來及制多所恭敬禮拜。復從如是一一化身，化出多手，或百或千，或過是數。此一切手皆持無量出過諸天上妙華香、殊勝可愛種種珍寶，奉散如來及制多所。復從如是一切化身，化出無量上妙音聲，歌讚如來廣大甚深真實功德。
items.en: Furthermore, when bodhisattvas make these offerings of wealth-and-respect veneration, vast veneration, and undefiled veneration to the Tathāgata and to shrines, the wealth used may come from wealth gathered through their own arms' labour, or wealth obtained by asking it of others, or the wealth of one who has attained mastery over requisites, all equally capable of accomplishing every kind of veneration described. A bodhisattva who has already attained mastery over requisites transforms and emanates manifestation-bodies, one, two, or many, even reaching hundreds of thousands or millions in number. Every one of these bodies bows and prostrates in reverence before the Tathāgata and every shrine. From each and every one of these manifestation-bodies in turn, many arms are further emanated, a hundred, a thousand, or more. Every one of these arms holds immeasurable, exquisite flowers and incense surpassing anything found even among the gods, and rare, beloved jewels of every kind, and scatters them in offering before the Tathāgata and every shrine. From all of these manifestation-bodies together, immeasurable, exquisite sounds are further emanated, singing the Tathāgata's vast, profound, and genuinely real qualities in praise.

items.zh: 復從如是一切化身，化出無量最上最妙環玔、璩印、寶莊嚴具，幢蓋、幡燈種種供具，供養如來及以制多。如是等類，已得眾具自在菩薩所設供養，皆屬自心。如是菩薩不更希求如來出世。何以故？由此菩薩已得證入不退轉地，一切佛土往來供養皆無礙故。

items.title: Section: Veneration Without Wealth — Rejoicing as the Great Equalizer, Available to Every Bodhisattva Regardless of Means

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，若無自力所集財寶，亦無從他求得財寶，及無菩薩所獲眾具自在財寶，可設供養；然於所有或贍部洲、或四大洲、或千世界、二千世界、或復三千大千世界，乃至十方無邊無際諸世界中，下中上品供養如來一切供具，菩薩於彼以淨信俱勝解俱心，周遍思惟，一切隨喜。如是菩薩少用功力，而興無邊廣大供養，攝受菩提廣大資糧。菩薩於此恒常無間起真善心、起歡喜心，當勤修學。
items.en: Furthermore, bodhisattvas who possess neither wealth gathered by their own labour, nor wealth obtained by asking others, nor the effortless wealth of a bodhisattva who has attained mastery over requisites, and thus have nothing available to offer — such bodhisattvas may nonetheless, with respect to every offering of every quality, lesser, middling, and superior, being made to the Tathāgata throughout Jambudvīpa, or the four great continents, or a thousand worlds, or two thousand worlds, or a great trichiliocosm of three thousand worlds, or indeed throughout every boundless, limitless world in the ten directions, join a mind of pure faith with a mind of genuine conviction, contemplate this universally, and rejoice in all of it without exception. Such bodhisattvas, expending very little effort, thereby raise up boundless, vast veneration, and gather in the vast provisions for awakening. Bodhisattvas should, without any interruption whatsoever, constantly raise this genuinely wholesome mind, this mind of joy, and should diligently train in doing so.

items.title: Section: Proper-Practice Veneration Opens — Five Practices Compressed Into the Time It Takes to Milk a Cow

items.zh: 若諸菩薩，少時少時、須臾須臾，乃至下如搆牛乳頃，普於一切蠢動有情修習慈悲喜捨俱心。於一切行修無常想、無常苦想、苦無我想。於其涅槃修勝利想，於佛法僧、波羅蜜多修習隨念；少時少時、須臾須臾，於一切法發生少分下劣忍智，信解離言法性真如，起無分別無相心住；何況於此若過若增。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who, for brief stretch after brief stretch, muhūrta after muhūrta, even for as short a span as it takes to draw a single pull of milk from a cow, cultivate throughout that span a mind joined with loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity towards every restlessly stirring being; who cultivate, towards all conditioned phenomena, the perception of impermanence, the perception of impermanence's own suffering, and the perception of suffering's own selflessness; who cultivate, towards nirvāṇa, the perception of its genuine benefit; who cultivate mindful recollection of the Buddha, the Dharma, the Saṅgha, and the perfections; and who, for brief stretch after brief stretch, muhūrta after muhūrta, generate towards all phenomena even a small measure of provisional patient acceptance and understanding, coming to have faith and comprehension in the true suchness of reality's own nature beyond all verbal expression, and thereby begin to settle the mind in a state free of conceptual discrimination and free of fixed characteristic — how much more so, then, should one expect of practising this even further and even more intensively.

blocks.text: The remaining kinds of veneration, ending with the one the treatise ranks highest. A short passage (0534b09) is untranslated.
Robes, food, bedding, medicine; inquiring respectfully, prostrating, circling clockwise. Master Cháng Bǎi: in prostration the five limbs touch the ground.
Offerings over a long time, abundant and exquisite. Venerable Miào Jìng: visualised offerings need the power of real concentration.

With one's own hands, without contempt; never while heedless or lazy; and "not smearing with orpiment, not bathing with ghee, not using guggulu incense or arka flowers or other impure substances" (Master Cháng Bǎi explains these Indian ritual substances).
Eighth-ground bodhisattvas venerate "with a hundred thousand hands" emanated in concentration (Venerable Miào Jìng).

"With a mind joined with pure faith, reflecting on all the offerings made to the Tathāgata in every world, and rejoicing in them." Venerable Miào Jìng: wealth obtained by asking others is the lowest; "without wealth, you needn't go asking; just sit and rejoice".
"Even for as short a span as it takes to milk a cow", cultivating loving-kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity. Venerable Miào Jìng: a xūyú, forty-eight minutes.

quiz.q: In wealth-and-respect veneration, what is "five-wheel prostration and circling to the right"?
options: prostrating with the five limbs and circumambulating clockwise
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the five "wheels" (limbs) touch the ground in prostration, and one circles the stūpa clockwise in reverence. Venerable Miào Jìng: five wheels are the five limbs.

quiz.q: In vast veneration, "pure mind and forceful conviction" — what level does Venerable Miào Jìng say makes it forceful?
options: there should be first-absorption concentration or higher, contemplating within it; scattered visualisation has no power
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: scattered visualisation has no power; there should be concentration of the first absorption or higher, contemplating within it — that is forceful conviction. Master Cháng Bǎi: vast veneration is achievable only by bodhisattvas of the first ground and above.

quiz.q: The sixth mark of undefiled veneration forbids offering what?
options: no orpiment smearing, no ghee bathing, no guggulu incense, arka flowers, or other impure things
quiz.why: "Not smearing with orpiment, not bathing with ghee, not using guggulu incense, arka flowers, or other impure substances." Master Cháng Bǎi: the first five concern an undefiled mind, the sixth the purity of the offerings.

quiz.q: "Bodhisattvas who have mastered requisites emanate bodies … with many hands" to make offerings. What stage, according to the lectures?
options: the eighth ground, with mastery of wealth; with the dharma body manifest, bodies are emanated from it
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: eighth-ground bodhisattvas have this mastery of wealth; with the dharma body manifest, they emanate bodies from it. Master Cháng Bǎi: bodhisattvas of the eighth ground and above obtain requisites at will.

quiz.q: A bodhisattva with no wealth at all to offer — what does the treatise say to do?
options: towards all offerings made anywhere in the ten directions, with pure faith and conviction, reflect on them and rejoice in all
quiz.why: Towards all offerings to the Tathāgata in every world, "with a mind joined with pure faith and conviction, reflecting on them all and rejoicing in all." Master Cháng Bǎi: visualising with pure faith and conviction is "little effort."

quiz.q: The treatise names three sources of wealth: own labour, asking others, mastery of requisites. How does Venerable Miào Jìng grade them?
options: wealth obtained by asking others is the lowest grade (own labour middle, mastery highest)
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: wealth obtained by asking others is the lowest grade; without wealth, "you needn't go asking — just sit in meditation more." (This grading is his own.)

quiz.q: Proper-practice veneration: for how brief a time, cultivating what?
options: even for the time of milking a cow, cultivating loving-kindness, compassion, joy, equanimity, and contemplations of impermanence, suffering, non-self
quiz.why: "Even for as short a span as it takes to milk a cow, cultivate a mind joined with loving-kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity towards every being, and contemplations of impermanence, suffering, non-self." Master Cháng Bǎi: kindness gives happiness, compassion removes suffering, joy rejoices in beings' good, equanimity teaches them to let go of greed and hatred.
